designs.title: No.
designs.why: The gag works: the deadpan cat lying across the word and batting the full stop like a ball reads in one glance, and the paw crossing the O ties the drawing and the type together. The confident brush line and one-colour woodcut feel suit an indie label and work on both white and black tees. What holds it back: the dense fine hatching on the tail reads grey from 3 m and will clog in one-ink screen print. The tail also hangs awkwardly into the N's margin, the hand-cut stripes in the letters look random rather than intentional, and the lockup is short and wide, so it sits small and high on the back.
designs.fix: Redraw the tail with fewer, heavier hatch lines (about half the density) and tuck it cleanly behind the N's left edge, so the silhouette stays crisp and printable at 3 m.
